why: Issue #222 asks that emergencies interrupt a held decision 'without making every shell or wall contact an immediate full reversal'. Treating ANY required escape as an emergency is the plausible-looking version of the rule that silently reinstates per-tick re-deciding for the whole time a tank is near a hazard -- which is where most reversals were measured. This mutates the MINE branch (the one that keeps a signed test); it is killed by the mine-shaped 'mildly off' fixture, which is deliberately not a bullet fixture, because the bullet branch returns exact opposite perpendiculars whose dot is only ever ~+1 or ~-1 and could never exercise that middle band.
killedBy: commitMove does NOT break the hold for an escape only mildly off the committed heading
